messages:
maria: Quick check-in — thinking about a long-running refactor to turn the current serving monolith into a small ‘ownership lattice’ of responsibilities. Not a full strangle, but smaller bounded nodes we can cut over. Thoughts on approach?
aj: Love the term 'ownership lattice' :) need to be explicit about runtime vs control-plane facts.
sachin: Agree. My main worry: data contracts and session ownership. Who owns persistent state vs ephemeral KV cache?
dana: Proposal: split along write-safety and hotpath latency. Hotpath runtime keeps ephemeral KV and LRU cache. Control plane owns config, model profiles, and rollout state.
maria: That's what I had in mind. Also want a gradual path: extract a "safety-net adapter" layer that owns fallbacks so we can route without a big switch.
nick: Can we enumerate the compatibility guarantees for the adapter? e.g., request shape, session token, headers. If we lock those we can do incremental cutovers.
leah: Suggestion: make a minimal shim API: POST /v1/infer -> translates to internal variants. Keep it idempotent for retries.
sachin: Implementation nit: use feature flags for routing so we can A/B tenant subsets. We should add a canary matrix: model, tenant, region.
addendum (infra-bot): New checklist created: refactor/ownership-lattice/checklist — assigns: @maria, @sachin.
maria: Good. For testing strategy: mock the adapter and run regression evals (prompt suites) to catch subtle deltas when we change quantized kernels.
aj: Also add perf gates: no change that increases p95 latency by >5% for hotpath percentiles. Accept smaller p50 tradeoffs only when cost falls >10%.
dana: On data ownership: control plane should expose a read-only projection of session meta to runtime. Runtime owns ephemeral commit semantics. This keeps consistency surface small.
nick: Does anyone foresee cross-service transaction needs? If so we should define compensating flows early.
sachin: We will avoid multi-service commits. If a request touches billing, control-plane will emit an event, but runtime won't block on it.
leah: Ops note: rollout runbook should include rollback via tenant shim toggle and traffic split to fallback model. Include probe that validates output shape and small eval metrics.
maria: Draft timeline: spike (2w) to implement adapter shim + routing flags, small canary (4w), expand to 20% traffic (2w), iterate on perf and regressions (ongoing).
aj: Can we publish a short RFC doc for this? one-pager with diagrams then spike tasks.
maria: Yes — I'll drop a RFC in google drive and link here. For now — volunteers for spike? @sachin and @nick?
sachin: I can take the adapter shim spike.
nick: I'll take routing and canary infra.
maria: Thanks — I'll update the checklist and the RFC later today. :thumbsup:
